explanation: Work from the last position toward index 1. At position i, choose uniformly from the still-unfixed prefix 0..i, using inclusive bounds, and swap that occurrence into i.
correctness: Before fixing i, the suffix after i is final and all other occurrences remain in 0..i. Each has conditional probability 1/(i+1) of being chosen. Multiplying n,n-1,...,2 choice probabilities gives 1/n! for every occurrence permutation.
walkthrough: For [4,8,1], start at i=2 and draw from 0..2. If chosen=0, swap to [1,8,4], fixing 4 at the end. At i=1, choose 0 or 1, producing [8,1,4] or [1,8,4]. Each full permutation has probability 1/(3*2)=1/6. The method returns no array; true is the adapter’s distribution and mutation verdict. The callable mutates the supplied array and returns void/None/undefined. Expected true is the checker verdict for occurrence preservation, identity, legal source use and unbiased permutations; it is not a particular array result.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays remain unchanged. Repeated values are separate occurrences; unbiased occurrence permutations may have the same visible value sequence.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: a constant-time random choice and swap fixes one position per iteration.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: only indices and a swap temporary; all rearrangement uses the original array.
